correctness.rationale: The exact independent-sample CDF is \(F_n(y)=(1-\exp(-\exp y))^n\), with quantile \(Q_n(u)=\log[-\log(1-u^{1/n})]\). Differentiation gives \(Q_n\prime(u)=h((-\log u)/n)/(u(-\log u))\). With \(t=\exp(-x)\) and \(a=-\log(1-t)\), strict elementary logarithmic inequalities imply both \(h\prime(x)>0\) and \((h(x)/x)\prime<0\), hence \(n/m<Q_m\prime(u)/Q_n\prime(u)<1\) for every \(u\in(0,1)\). The limits \(h(x)\sim x\) as \(x\to\infty\) and \(h(x)\sim1/\log(1/x)\) as \(x\downarrow0\) prove sharp endpoint constants. Integration yields strict interquantile bounds; a uniform-quantile coupling gives all positive-order distance inequalities and the variance bounds; the integrated-quantile criterion gives centered convex order. All needed log moments exist. The standalone finite checker passed 9,264 diagnostics; the proof is analytic.

value.rationale: All quantile widths, not merely variance, are natural measures of uncertainty for minima of independent coupon-collector completion limits. Exact best global transport Lipschitz constants \(n/m\) and \(1\) describe genuine asymmetric tail sensitivity, while pairwise spread domination and centered convex order control entire classes of uncertainty functionals. These statements are mathematically stronger than the covered scalar decrease and are useful without a separate downstream theorem.
